Why do some groups of talented people accomplish extraordinary things together, while other groups of equally talented people become slow, political, or frustrated? And how do we deliberately build the first kind?

Seeking.com is the world's largest premium dating platform, founded by an MIT alumnus and headquartered in Las Vegas. STNDRDS is our consumer media brand; Standards.com is our independent news publication. Together we are a combined US operating organization built on one premise: we exist to create value for the people we serve, not to extract it from them.
We are 50 to 60 people, split between our Las Vegas office and remote roles across the country, and we intend to stay small by design. We grow through leverage per person, not headcount. That makes how our people are selected, organized, and work together the single biggest determinant of what we can accomplish.
The Opportunity
You own the design and effectiveness of the human operating system of the company: what people and structure we need, how we select them, how we organize, develop, and reward them, and how they work together. You are not here to administer HR programs. You are here to make the organization, and every person in it, more effective.
The core question you carry every day:
Do we have the right people, organized the right way, operating under the right conditions and incentives, to accomplish what we are asking the company to accomplish?
When the answer is no, you diagnose before you prescribe. Is it the person, the manager, the structure, the incentives, the team composition, unclear ownership, decision rights, information flow, missing capability, or something nobody else has noticed? Then you design the smallest intervention that fixes the real cause, and you measure whether it worked.
Three ideas shape how we work. The Value Creator System: people earn gain share based on demonstrated repeatable value. The Certainty Framework: design work to create the conditions for eustress (voluntary striving toward something you care about) and remove structural sources of distress. General Information
The Pacific Legal Foundation identifies and litigates important legal issues to set landmark precedents that benefit Americans nationwide. Using strategic and principled litigation, communications, and research, PLF battles for freedom in the nation’s capitols, courts, and the court of public opinion.
 
As a national nonprofit law firm, PLF has brick-and-mortar offices in Sacramento, California; Arlington, Virginia; and Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, although approximately half of the staff work from home offices across the country. Interns work remotely by default, but they can request to work physically in any of PLF’s offices. Interns are expected to work part time (24 hours per week).

PLF has an unmatched record in the U.S. Supreme Court, with 18 victories out of 21 cases heard by the Court. PLF also has nearly 200 active cases across the nation. Since 2024, PLF’s state-policy team has capitalized on our Supreme Court wins and helped pass 96 bills across 41 states by testifying, refining bill language, and guiding local allies toward victory. At PLF, we aren’t interested in doing the same thing as everyone else. We aspire to be the best player in a constantly changing game.
 
As a member of the State Policy team, you will work with all PLF’s capabilities-litigation, strategic research, coalitions, and communications-to draft legislation, model bills, one-pagers, research memos, and blogs and op-eds supporting our mission and vision.
 
Your specific job duties will likely include:
Conducting legislative and other research to support policy drafting

Curiosity about the law and public policy

Strong writing and research skills

If you think you might be a good fit, submit in ONE PDF:
A résumé that includes relevant experience in the liberty movement and professional skills.
A cover letter explaining why PLF is the place for you, why you want to fight for liberty, and what distinguishes you from typical applicants.

A writing sample.
A semester schedule (if taking classes during the internship period).
